title: Per-customer change-triggered regression gatekeeper with local hashed anchors
creator: Marco Chen
description: Implement a per-customer, change-triggered regression gatekeeper that runs short, privacy-preserving evals whenever a model binary or serving configuration change is deployed for Dedicated/Private customers. The gatekeeper must run using customer-scoped anchor prompt sets that never leave the customer's VPC or onboarding bundle: only compact, hashed digests and differential metrics are transmitted to the control plane. The feature should provide a conservative default threshold to block rollouts that cause >X% regression on customer-specific quality signals and allow opt-in relaxed policies. This ticket covers product requirements, success metrics, rollout policy, and UX surface in the Console for visibility and manual override.
acceptance_criteria: Trigger: Any model version change, quantization profile change, kernel-selection update, or serving-runtime config change invokes the gatekeeper for affected customers within the rollout window.

Customer anchors: The system supports per-customer anchor sets (small prompt/response pairs) that remain encrypted/inbound-only in customer Dedicated or Private deployments; Redwood only receives hashed anchors and aggregated deltas.

Privacy guarantees: No raw customer prompts/responses leave the customer environment. Telemetry is limited to deterministic hashes, bucketed score deltas, and non-identifying histograms; PII scan applied before any telemetry export.

Gating: Gatekeeper computes regression score and blocks automated rollout if regression exceeds configurable threshold; console shows blocked rollout with root-cause indicators and link to replay details (local only).

Visibility: Console shows per-customer pre/post metrics (token-level latency, top-k accuracy proxies, hallucination proxy rate) and a concise verdict (Pass/Fail/Manual-Review) within 15 minutes of gate execution.
Operator controls: Customers and Redwood operators can configure thresholds per-customer, set automatic rollback or manual hold, and opt-out entirely; changes are audited.
Performance: Per-customer eval runs complete within configured SLO (default 10 minutes) and do not materially affect serving capacity (isolated eval pool or scheduled pouching).
Integrations: Workflows integrate with existing rollouts/canary APIs so blocked deployments cancel canary expansion and surface remediation steps.
Docs and runbook: Shipping includes Console UX copy, onboarding checklist for customers (how to provision anchors), and an on-call runbook for investigating false positives.
Security review: Feature design has passed security review and conforms to KMS/HSM key usage for any exported digests when required by customer settings.
notes: 2026-02-22: Initial scoping completed with Eng (serving, infra) and Security. Agreed to use local hashed anchors and differential metrics to minimize data egress.
2026-03-01: Eng proposed an isolated eval worker pool tied to Dedicated capacity reservations to avoid impacting production latency; product to define SLOs and cost model.
2026-03-05: Design review: console flow should default to 'Preview mode' showing expected delta before enabling automatic blocking; added manual override path.
Trade-offs: Short eval suites reduce coverage but keep cost and latency manageable; we will offer a longer 'deep-check' run as a post-approval optional job.
Compliance note: For Private/on-prem, eval orchestration runs wholly in-customer environment; Redwood provides the orchestrator artifact but no raw data extraction.
qa_plan: Unit tests for hashing/aggregation logic and telemetry redaction in staging
Integration tests: simulate model/config change and validate gate decisions using synthetic customer anchors
E2E: Deploy to a Dedicated test customer, validate no raw anchors leave VPC and console verdicts match expected thresholds
Chaos test: network partition during eval run should surface 'unknown' verdict and not silently pass a rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): Opt-in Redwood test customers and internal Dedicated clusters. Manual gating, detailed observability enabled.
Phase 2 (beta): Invite early enterprise customers; enable automatic blocking with conservative thresholds and human-in-loop notifications.
Phase 3 (GA): Default enable for Dedicated customers with per-customer thresholds and self-serve anchor onboarding; Private customers get orchestrator artifact and local-only mode.
Fallbacks: If gate fails or is unavailable, rollout respects configured fallback policy (manual hold or allow with alert).
risks: False positives could block safe rollouts causing customer downtime; require conservative defaults and easy override.
Eval cost for many customers could be significant without batching/pooled eval infra; need cost attribution and quota controls.
Potential complexity for on-prem deployment upgrades if orchestrator version mismatch occurs; include compatibility matrix in docs.
